fields.h1: Build a Supplement Quiz That Matches Shoppers to Your Products
fields.hero_description: Build a supplement quiz that matches shoppers to products by how they like to take them, or try the eight-question one below.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Supplement Quiz on Emergent
fields.features_subheading: A supplement quiz sorts shoppers into the formats you stock. Emergent builds the questions and the table behind them.
fields.feature_1:
Results named after the formats you sell

List the formats on your shelf, such as capsules and gummies. Emergent writes the questions so that every option counts toward one of them, and you reword any question by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Your products on each result screen

Tag each product in the app's product table with the result it suits and a diet label, such as vegan. The result screen lists the tagged items, and a retag shows on the next quiz.
fields.feature_3:
Medicine questions handed to a person

Add a question about prescription medicines, and a Yes skips the product list. The app emails your pharmacist a link, and the answers stay in the database, out of the inbox.
fields.feature_4:
A conversational flow sized for a thumb

Emergent builds the quiz as a conversational flow with one question per screen. A shopper holding a phone in the store aisle can answer all eight and see a result before checkout.
fields.feature_5:
Every finished quiz kept as a row

Each result, the options picked, and an email when one is given save as one row in a database you own. Filter by Powders to see what time of day those shoppers take one.
fields.feature_6:
On your domain, with code you can keep

Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits, so the quiz can sit at your store's address. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep it.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Shops Running a Supplement Quiz
fields.tab_content_1:
For a Gummies result, the vegan gummies come first

Sarafina Duvernay answers eight questions on Vesperline Nutrition's site and lands on Gummies. Her result screen lists the 3 vegan gummies the company tagged for that format, starting with its daily multivitamin. Her answers and email are stored in Vesperline's shopper table.
fields.tab_content_2:
When a shopper takes a prescription, the pharmacist steps in

Every quiz at the Copperwell Pharmacy counter asks whether the shopper takes a prescription medicine. A Yes ends on "Ask our pharmacist" instead of a product list. Pharmacist Zuleika Amaro gets an email that says a quiz is in, with a link and no answers in it.
fields.tab_content_3:
Refill email at day 25 of a 30-day tub

Each subscriber at Saltmeadow Daily gets a 30-day supply in the format their quiz result named. Iduna Kincaid landed on Powders, so a tub ships to her each month. On day 25, the app emails her a refill reminder, 5 days before the tub runs out, with a link to skip a month or switch formats.
fields.tab_content_4:
In the fall, capsules led with 480 of 1,200

A tablet by the register at Bramblecrest Market runs the supplement quiz. This fall, 1,200 shoppers finished it: Capsules led with 480, then Gummies at 360, Powders at 220, and Liquids at 140. Owner Ferdinand Tavakoli doubled the capsule shelf.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Supplement Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a supplement quiz that matches each shopper to a format and leaves health questions to a person.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Tag every product to one result
fields.howto_step_1_des: Settle the results before writing a question. The FDA says supplements come in forms such as pills, capsules, gummies, liquids, and powders. Pick the four your shelf carries most, and every result can end on something a shopper can buy today.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write questions about how people like to take a supplement: whether pills feel like a chore, what time of day suits them, where the bottle will live. Those answers point to a format without asking about a single symptom or condition.
fields.howto_step_3_des: If you ask about prescription medicines, leave that question out of the scoring. Let a Yes end on a screen that names your pharmacist, or that asks the shopper to check with their doctor first, never on a product list.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give each product in the app's table one result and any diet labels it carries, such as vegan or gluten-free. Three products per result screen let a shopper compare a few instead of scrolling the whole catalog.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Open each result on the format and the answers that led to it, then the products. Close with the FDA's advice to consult a health care professional before deciding to take a dietary supplement, in plain type, not fine print.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Play it as four different shoppers
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before launch, take the quiz yourself four times, once as each kind of shopper. If an honest set of answers lands on the wrong format, the question meant to split them is too vague. Rewrite it and play again.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Once a month, set each format's result count beside what sold. A format that wins the quiz but stays on the shelf points to price or placement. A format nobody lands on may not need a result of its own.

faq_plan.a: A supplement quiz is a short set of questions that matches a shopper to a supplement product or format. The quiz on this page asks only how you like to take one, and its result names a format: capsules, gummies, powders, or liquids.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a supplement quiz?
faq_plan.a: Describe the formats you sell and how each result should end, and Emergent's AI survey builder writes the questions and the table that stores every answer. Add a pharmacist alert or refill emails by prompt before you publish.

faq_plan.q: Should a supplement quiz ask about health conditions?
faq_plan.a: No. Keep a store's supplement quiz to habits and preferences, such as format and taste. A question about a condition invites a product match that reads as medical advice. Point anyone with a health question to a pharmacist or doctor instead.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a supplement quiz have?
faq_plan.a: Eight works well for a supplement quiz with four results: two questions per format, short enough to finish on a phone. Past ten, cut the question nearly everyone answers the same way. Emergent puts no cap on how many shoppers take it.

faq_plan.q: Can a supplement quiz show products from my own store?
faq_plan.a: It can: tag each product in your catalog to one result, and the result screen lists those items. The app can also connect to your store platform through its API, which keeps the price and stock on each result screen in step with the catalog.

faq_plan.q: Should a supplement quiz ask about prescription medicines?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when a pharmacist or doctor can follow up. The FDA notes that some supplements might interact with medicines or other supplements. Leave the answer out of the score, and send a Yes to a person rather than a product list.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep supplement quiz answers private?
faq_plan.a: Keep the answers in one place and out of messages. Answers save to a database you own, and an alert can carry a link to the record instead of the answers. Emergent has SOC 2 Type I and ISO 27001.

faq_plan.q: Can a supplement quiz filter for vegan or gluten-free products?
faq_plan.a: It can: ask one diet question and leave it out of the score. The result screen then lists only products tagged with that label, and a format with no match says so instead of showing the closest item.

faq_plan.q: Where should the email field go in a supplement quiz?
faq_plan.a: Put it after the result, as an optional field. Say in one line what you will send, such as a copy of the result or refill reminders, and store the address in the same row as the result.

faq_plan.q: How do I tell if my supplement quiz is working?
faq_plan.a: Check two numbers each month: how many who start the quiz finish it, and how each result's count compares with what sold. A drop at one question points to that question. Emergent rewrites it from a prompt the same day.

quiz.title: Which Supplement Format Fits Your Routine?
quiz.intro: Eight questions about how you like to take a supplement. Your result names the format your answers lean toward. It is not medical advice: ask a pharmacist or doctor what to take.

questions.text: How do you feel about swallowing a pill?

options.text: No trouble at all
I would rather chew something
I would rather drink it
A spoonful or a few drops suits me

questions.text: When in the day would you most likely take it?

options.text: With breakfast and a glass of water
As an afternoon snack
Blended into a morning smoothie
Stirred into juice or tea

questions.text: Where will it live day to day?

options.text: In the bathroom cabinet
In a desk drawer or a bag
On the counter by the blender
In the fridge door

questions.text: How much does taste matter to you?

options.text: I want no taste at all
A fruit flavor makes it easier
I like a flavor I can mix into a drink
A mild taste is fine if it is quick

questions.text: How do you like to take it with you when you travel?

options.text: A small bottle in my carry-on
A pouch I can open anywhere
Single-serve stick packs
I mostly take it at home

questions.text: Which container would you rather keep?

options.text: A bottle with a count on the label
A resealable pouch or jar
A tub with a scoop
A bottle with a dropper or measuring cap

questions.text: How do you like to start a new habit?

options.text: Make it as short as a sip of water
Make it feel like a treat
Fold it into a drink I already make
Keep it to one quick spoonful

questions.text: Which sounds most like your morning?

options.text: Coffee, keys, and out the door
Breakfast eaten on the go
The blender running most days
A slow cup of tea at the table

results.title: Capsules and Tablets
results.description: Your answers lean toward a format that takes seconds with a glass of water and has no taste. Ask the store which capsules carry the diet labels you need, and check with a pharmacist or doctor before you start one.

results.title: Gummies
results.description: Your answers lean toward something you chew, with a flavor that makes the habit easier to keep. Ask which gummies carry the diet labels you need, such as vegan, and check with a pharmacist or doctor before you start one.

results.title: Powders You Mix
results.description: Your answers lean toward a format you stir or blend into a drink you already make. Look at single-serve packs if you travel, and check with a pharmacist or doctor before you add one to your routine.

results.title: Liquids
results.description: Your answers lean toward a spoonful or a few drops, taken at home and stirred into juice or tea if you like. Ask which liquids carry the diet labels you need, and check with a pharmacist or doctor before you start one.

plan.angle: The top 10 is supplement brands' own finders and health-library vitamin quizzes, and every one asks about health to name a product, which is advice a store quiz should not give. This page gives a visitor an eight-question supplement quiz they can take right here that matches them to a format (capsules, gummies, powders, or liquids) by how they like to take one, never by symptoms, and then shows four businesses running their own: a vitamin brand showing the products it tagged for each result, a pharmacy that sends any prescription answer to the pharmacist, a subscription brand timing refill reminders, and a market restocking from result counts. Every answer stays in a database the owner keeps, and the FAQ covers wording, privacy, medication questions, and what a result screen should say.
